problem: Existing indoor navigation methods represent each key location by a panorama's visual features or by an unweighted object list, which is unreliable under illumination change, shadows and repeated objects across rooms, and loses geometric/orientation information needed for positioning and path planning.
motivation: Indoor scenes contain visually similar rooms (offices, meeting rooms), so treating all objects as equally important gives poor localization. A compact, navigation-specific scene summary that keeps salient objects, their context and their angular layout could support both localization and heading estimation.
key_idea: Represent each panorama RGB-D scene as a 360° saliency graph (volumetric-saliency objects as nodes, contextual edges with saliency-derived weights, and azimuth angles/3D positions as geometry), then localize by graph matching and estimate shift and orientation by geometric alignment of matched nodes.
insight: The ablation shows monotone localization gains as information is added: image features 0.68, objects 0.76, salient objects 0.82, unweighted saliency graph 0.84, full 360° saliency graph 0.86. Larger FOV also helps (0.37 at 60° to 0.91 at 360°). Adding graph-based positioning to navigation lifts SR from 58.73 to 76.92. Caveat: navigation results use the paper's own pipeline, so the comparison to baselines is not like-for-like.
method: Topological map: nodes are scene points plus scene-transition points detected on region-mask boundaries (boundary connectivity) within obstruction-free floor areas; edges from a visibility graph; relative azimuths between nodes stored; Floyd-Warshall gives shortest paths.

360° saliency graph construction: objects detected in the panorama, salient ones selected via volumetric saliency; nodes are salient objects; edge exists if min(mean dimensions) > spatial distance; edge weight sqrt(S_a*S_b); each node stores azimuth (and polar) angle of its centroid, 3D position and saliency score.

Scene localization: Jaccard similarity picks candidate graphs (>0.6 × max); node alignment via node2vec features + label + saliency; edge-triplet matching score sum(W∘M); best-scoring graph gives the node location.

Position estimation: least-squares shift Δ between the query and matched graph reference points from matched node positions, Δ = ½ B† b (Theorem 1, using distance invariance and pairwise differences).
Orientation alignment: after shifting, per-node azimuth differences are averaged with saliency weights to get the alignment angle θ̂.

Navigation loop: localize, align, rotate toward the next node on the shortest path, move, and repeat at each intermediate node; for REVERIE, the graph localization replaces the room-type prediction in MiC (March-in-Chat).

setting.backbone: Graph matching with pre-existing object detector [guerrero2020s] and volumetric saliency; MiC (CLIP-based) for the REVERIE navigation policy; ResNet-101 only in the image-feature ablation baseline
setting.training_data: No new training for localization/positioning (hand-designed graph matching); MiC policy is reused from prior work
setting.observation: Panoramic RGB-D images (Matterport3D), rendered with Blender for shifted views
setting.action_space: Discrete topological-map nodes; rotate toward and move to the next node on the shortest path
setting.simulator: Matterport3D (with Blender rendering for perturbed views); MATLAB implementation
setting.privileged: Pre-built topological map with reference panoramas/graphs for all locations (region/object semantic masks and floor map from Habitat-map method); all methods use the same global topological map

numbers.backbone: MiC with saliency-graph localization replacing room-type prediction

numbers_note: Data split for REVERIE is not stated; the main navigation comparison replaces MiC's room prediction only, and the 76.92 SR result is not explained in detail. Pose estimation on 105 synthetic test images: mean position error 0.6995 m, orientation error 16.59°.
results: Localization accuracy is 0.86 versus 0.82 for SOVS and 0.80 for MFP-CNN, and MMA@3 is 87.8 versus 49.82 for the best feature-matching baseline. Swapping the graph localization into MiC on REVERIE raises OSR/SR/SPL from 62.37/56.97/43.60 to 66.78/59.78/48.66, and the full pipeline reaches SR 76.92 / SPL 72.85.
limitations: Degrades in dynamic environments with rapid scene changes; heavy object perturbation (66%) drops navigation SR to 40.28.

Evaluated in a custom Matterport3D-based topological-map setup that relies on a pre-built map with known reference graphs, GT-style region/object masks, and MATLAB, so it is not a standard VLN protocol comparison.
Localization accuracy falls with building size (0.82 at 106 rooms), and the numbers come from a single-author-run comparison without variance.
builds_on: Indoor saliency graph matching (Meena et al. 2024)
